knowledge.explanation: A prefix's occupied set determines exactly the first available space for every next preference, while its maximum and the new displacement determine the updated maximum. Appending a is a bijection from prefixes counted by a given state to successful extensions associated with that state and a. Different state/preference triples give disjoint ordered tuples because deleting the final entry recovers the preceding prefix and its unique state. Conversely every successful extension has such a deletion. Induction from the unique empty prefix proves the invariant for all t<=n; at t=n the occupied set must be [n], giving the terminal counts. Failed arrivals have no successful extensions and contribute nothing. The empty maximum convention is valid because all displacements are nonnegative; n=1 produces [1]. recurrence.md gives the complete argument and bit-mask correspondence. This is a nonformal proved counting mechanism, without a claim of all-n unimodality or Lean certification.
knowledge.statement: For every n>=1, let D_t(S,m) count successful ordered length-t preference prefixes in [n]^t with occupied set S and maximum displacement m, with empty-prefix maximum 0. Initialize D_0(empty,0)=1. For each a in [n], if p=min([a,n] minus S) exists, add D_t(S,m) to D_{t+1}(S union {p},max(m,p-a)); otherwise add nothing. Then b[n,k]=D_n([n],k) for every 0<=k<n.
knowledge.summary: A direct prefix-counting proof justifies an exact state recurrence for arbitrary n, independently of published formulas; shape inequalities remain open.
knowledge.title: Occupied-set recurrence for exact maximum parking displacement
